beats: Every wall lesson had to fill five steps, even when a topic ran out of material after three.
That left kids answering padded, repeated questions that taught nothing new, just to hit the count.
Now the planner can skip a thin step -- but only if Claude's editor agrees the material is truly exhausted.
A lazy shortcut gets rejected and sent back for a real step instead.
Lessons now run three to five cards -- as many as the topic actually earns.
